description: Curriculum layer — structured foundation phase, explicit teaching moments, and frequency-weighted vocabulary ordering. All logic-only, no visual/rendering changes.

userStories.title: Alphabet mastery progression engine
userStories.description: Build a structured alphabet learning sequence that gates the rest of the game. Players must demonstrate recognition of all 28 Arabic letters (isolated, initial, medial, final forms) before the sandbox opens. Track per-letter mastery with FSRS cards.
acceptanceCriteria: src/store/slices/alphabetProgressSlice.js tracks mastery per letter (28 consonants + 6 vowels)
Each letter has 4 form states: isolated, initial, medial, final — each tracked independently
getLetterMastery(letterId) returns mastery percentage across all 4 forms
isAlphabetComplete(state) returns true when all letters at 80%+ mastery
Letter introduction order follows standard AFL sequence (Alif Baa textbook order)
selectNextLettersToLearn(state, count) returns next unlearned letters in sequence
alphabetGateMiddleware blocks zone entry dispatches until isAlphabetComplete is true
Tests: 16+ tests covering per-letter tracking, form states, gate logic, completion check
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read arabicPhonetics.js for letter data. Read settingsSlice.js for showDiacritics. Standard AFL order: أ ب ت ث ج ح خ د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ع غ ف ق ك ل م ن ه و ي. Gate should be skippable if placement test shows existing knowledge.

userStories.title: Core 100 high-frequency word set with explicit teaching data
userStories.description: Create an ordered set of the 100 most essential Arabic words for beginners, each with explicit teaching data: word, root, meaning, example sentence, pronunciation guide, mnemonic hint, and FSRS card. These are introduced sequentially after alphabet mastery, before the sandbox opens.
acceptanceCriteria: src/data/coreVocabulary.js exports ordered array of 100 words
Each word has: arabic, english, root (trilateral), rootMeaning, exampleSentence, pronunciationGuide, mnemonicHint, category, frequencyRank
Categories covered: greetings (10), pronouns (8), basic verbs (15), numbers (10), family (8), food (8), directions (8), time (8), common nouns (15), adjectives (10)
getNextCoreWords(completedCount, batchSize) returns next N words in sequence
isCoreVocabComplete(state) returns true when all 100 words at 70%+ mastery
selectCoreVocabProgress(state) returns { completed, total, percentage }
Tests: 12+ tests covering data completeness, ordering, category coverage, progress tracking
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Use frequency data from established Arabic word lists. Words should be MSA. Root field connects to the root system teaching in FEAT-043. Each word must exist in vocabularyExpanded.js — cross-reference by wordId.

userStories.title: Trilateral root system teaching engine
userStories.description: Build an explicit root system introduction that teaches the Arabic trilateral root concept early. Show how one root generates multiple related words. Track root knowledge separately from individual word knowledge. This is Arabic's vocabulary multiplier.
acceptanceCriteria: src/data/rootTeachingSet.js exports 30 common roots with derived word families
Each root entry: root (3 letters), coreMeaning, derivedWords [{arabic, english, pattern, form}] (4-6 words per root)
src/store/slices/rootKnowledgeSlice.js tracks known roots and mastery
learnRoot(rootId) marks root as introduced
getRootMastery(rootId) calculates mastery from derived word FSRS scores
selectKnownRoots(state) returns all roots player has been taught
predictWordFromRoot(root, pattern) pure function returns expected word — teaches pattern recognition
Root teaching integrated into foundation phase: 5 roots introduced after first 20 core words
Tests: 14+ tests covering root data, mastery calculation, prediction logic, teaching sequence
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read existing root-related code — rootMagicSlice.js, rootFsrsSyncMiddleware.js. Common roots: ك-ت-ب (writing), د-ر-س (studying), ع-ل-م (knowledge), etc. Root teaching should feel like a superpower discovery, not a grammar lesson.

userStories.title: Foundation phase orchestrator
userStories.description: Build the orchestrator that sequences the foundation phase: alphabet → core vocabulary → root system introduction. Gates the open sandbox until foundation milestones are met. Tracks overall foundation progress and handles placement test bypass.
acceptanceCriteria: src/store/slices/foundationSlice.js tracks foundation phase state
Foundation stages: alphabet → coreVocab → rootIntro → complete
getCurrentFoundationStage(state) returns current stage
advanceFoundationStage() moves to next stage when current is complete
Completion criteria: alphabet 80%+, core vocab 70%+ on first 50 words, 5 roots introduced
Placement test bypass: if placement score > A1, skip to sandbox (foundation marked complete)
foundationMiddleware enforces stage gates — blocks actions that require later stages
selectFoundationProgress(state) returns { stage, stageProgress, overallProgress }
Tests: 14+ tests covering stage progression, gates, bypass, progress calculation
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read placementSlice.js for placement test state. This orchestrates FEAT-041, 042, 043 into a coherent flow. Foundation should feel like the game's prologue, not a test.

userStories.title: Zone vocabulary pre-teaching data
userStories.description: For each of the 8 zones, create a curated set of 10-15 key words that players are explicitly taught before exploring that zone. Each word includes the root, a zone-contextual example, and a brief explanation. This is the 'brief explicit teaching moment' before contextual learning.
acceptanceCriteria: src/data/zoneVocabIntros.js exports zone-keyed object with 8 zones
Each zone has 10-15 words: arabic, english, root, zoneContext (why this word matters here), exampleInZone
Words selected by relevance to zone theme (marketplace = commerce, library = academic, etc.)
getZoneIntroWords(zoneId) returns the teaching set for that zone
isZoneIntroComplete(zoneId, state) checks if player has reviewed all intro words
selectZoneIntroProgress(zoneId) returns { reviewed, total, percentage }
Total: 80-100 unique words across all 8 zones (some overlap allowed for high-frequency words)
Tests: 12+ tests covering all zones have data, word structure, progress tracking
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read zones.js for zone IDs and themes. Cross-reference with vocabularyExpanded.js to use existing word IDs. Zone themes: Oasis Village (basics), Desert Marketplace (commerce), Sacred Library (academic), Mountain Pass (nature/travel), Coastal Port (trade/foreign), Garden District (food/plants), Ancient Ruins (history), Bedouin Camp (culture/hospitality).

userStories.title: Zone intro teaching middleware
userStories.description: Create middleware that triggers the explicit teaching moment when a player enters a zone for the first time (or hasn't completed the zone's intro). Presents zone vocabulary words one at a time with root, meaning, and context before the player can freely explore.
acceptanceCriteria: zoneIntroMiddleware intercepts world/enterZone actions
On first zone entry: dispatches zoneIntro/start with the zone's teaching words
Tracks which words have been reviewed per zone in zoneIntroSlice
presentNextIntroWord(zoneId) returns next unreviewed word with full teaching data
completeIntroWord(zoneId, wordId) marks word as reviewed, creates FSRS card
Zone intro can be dismissed early (player choice) but shows progress reminder
Re-entering zone after dismissal resumes where player left off
Tests: 14+ tests covering first entry trigger, word progression, dismissal, resume, FSRS card creation
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read zoneEntryReviewMiddleware.js for zone entry interception pattern. This is different from micro-review — this is for FIRST entry teaching, micro-review is for returning visits with due cards. Create zoneIntroSlice.js for state.

userStories.title: Frequency-weighted vocabulary ordering
userStories.description: Add frequency rank data to all vocabulary and create a weighted selection function that biases new word introduction toward higher-frequency words. Within each CEFR level, words are introduced roughly by frequency rank rather than randomly.
acceptanceCriteria: frequencyRank field added to vocabulary data (rank 1 = most common, higher = less common)
At minimum, top 500 words have accurate frequency ranks from established Arabic frequency lists
getFrequencyWeightedNewCards(availableCards, count) selects new cards biased toward lower rank numbers
Weighting: rank 1-500 = 3x selection weight, 501-1000 = 2x, 1001-2000 = 1.5x, 2000+ = 1x
Integrates with existing getNewCardsForSession in fsrs.js — frequency weighting applied before path ordering
selectVocabByFrequencyTier(state) returns counts per tier for progress display
Tests: 14+ tests covering weighted selection distribution, tier counting, integration with FSRS
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read vocabularyExpanded.js for current word structure. Read fsrs.js getNewCardsForSession. Frequency data source: use established MSA frequency lists. Don't reorder existing FSRS due cards — only affect NEW card introduction order.

userStories.title: Grammar scaffolding data tied to zones
userStories.description: Create grammar teaching points mapped to zones. Each zone introduces 2-3 grammar concepts that are relevant to that zone's content. Grammar is taught just-in-time when the player needs it, not in abstract sequence.
acceptanceCriteria: src/data/zoneGrammarPoints.js exports zone-keyed grammar teaching data
Each zone has 2-3 grammar points: concept, explanation (simple English), arabicExample, pattern, relatedVocab
Grammar concepts ordered by natural progression across zones (present tense before past, singular before plural, etc.)
getZoneGrammar(zoneId) returns grammar points for that zone
isGrammarPointLearned(pointId, state) checks if player has completed the grammar exercise
selectGrammarProgress(state) returns { learned, total, byZone }
Total: 16-24 grammar points across 8 zones covering A1-B1 grammar
Tests: 12+ tests covering data structure, zone coverage, progression tracking, grammar ordering
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: Read grammar.js for existing grammar data. Zone 1-2 grammar: basic sentence structure, present tense, pronouns. Zone 3-4: past tense, plurals, possession. Zone 5-6: future, conditionals, comparatives. Zone 7-8: passive, subjunctive, complex sentences.

userStories.title: Explicit teaching session service
userStories.description: Build the service that powers explicit vocabulary teaching moments. Given a word with its teaching data (root, meaning, context, mnemonic), it creates a structured 4-step teaching sequence: see → hear → connect → practice. Returns structured session data for the UI to render.
acceptanceCriteria: createTeachingSession(word) returns structured session with 4 steps
Step 1 (See): word in Arabic with diacritics, English meaning, transliteration
Step 2 (Hear): pronunciation data reference, word broken into syllables
Step 3 (Connect): root + root meaning + 2 related words from same root
Step 4 (Practice): generate a simple recognition question (pick this word from 4 options)
generateDistractors(targetWord, allVocab, count) returns plausible wrong answers
completeTeachingSession(wordId) creates FSRS card with initial Good rating
Distractor selection: same CEFR level, same category, visually distinct Arabic
Tests: 14+ tests covering session structure, distractor quality, FSRS card creation, all 4 steps
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: This is the core service that FEAT-046 (zone intros) and the foundation phase use. Pure functions that return data — no UI rendering. Distractors should not share the same root as the target word.

userStories.title: Curriculum progress dashboard data service
userStories.description: Build a service that aggregates all curriculum progression data into a single dashboard-ready object. Combines foundation progress, zone intro progress, vocabulary tiers, grammar coverage, root knowledge, and CEFR estimates into one comprehensive view.
acceptanceCriteria: getCurriculumDashboard(state) returns complete progress object

Dashboard includes: foundationPhase (stage, progress), zonesIntroduced (per zone completion), vocabTiers (count per frequency tier), grammarCoverage (learned/total per zone), rootKnowledge (known roots, derived words unlocked), cefrEstimate (overall + per skill)
selectCurriculumDashboard(state) memoized selector for Redux
estimateTimeToNextCefr(currentProgress) returns hours estimate based on current pace
getWeakAreas(dashboard) identifies lowest-progress areas for recommendation
suggestNextActivity(dashboard) returns recommended next action (study roots, review zone vocab, practice grammar, etc.)
Tests: 12+ tests covering aggregation accuracy, time estimation, weak area detection, recommendations
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: This reads from foundationSlice, alphabetProgressSlice, rootKnowledgeSlice, zoneIntroSlice, vocabularySlice, and cefrProgressSlice. Pure aggregation — no mutations. Time estimates extrapolate from FSRS review pace.
